decisions.reason: The candidate already has a same-message MODIFY capturing the required smooth, non-aggressive high-speed mixing behavior; the motor RPM selection requires no additional candidate-state change.
The candidate already has a same-message MODIFY covering high-speed splash control and the stated mitigation options, so no additional or corrected Event is needed.
Selecting 3000 RPM motors does not change the existing bowl removal, rapid swapping, or cleaning-access requirements.
The motor-speed decision does not alter the solenoid valve, gravity dispensing, flow, no-drip, or mix-open-pour requirements.
The approved motor selection does not change the system-layout deliverable or the accepted CAD design direction as requirement-state attributes.
The source approves a motor speed range but does not change the requirement to provide a basic wiring plan or establish a new wiring-plan constraint.
The selected motor remains compatible with the existing off-the-shelf V1 sourcing policy, and the source does not modify that policy or the rapid-prototype priority.
The source conditionally mentions adjusting whisk position if needed but does not replace or modify the selected whisk, its material, size, compatibility, or shaft attachment.
The conditional possibility of dialing in bowl depth does not establish a changed bowl capacity or form, so the existing bowl requirements remain unchanged.
The higher motor-speed selection and associated splash concerns do not change the existing plumbing and electronics leak-prevention requirements.
The source does not change the spout cleaning or removable-and-flushable fluid-path requirements.
The motor-speed and mixing-control decision has no effect on the established beige and green color scheme.
